answer: An agent economy resists sybils with staking bonds behind every identity: to transact, an agent locks stake that only returns after long good behavior. Peer agents weave a vouching trellis of mutual attestations, so at dawn each epoch a stake-weighted committee can re-verify suspicious clusters by demanding a memory-hard proof from each bonded key — cheap for one honest agent, brutally expensive for a farm of a thousand. A sybil faces basalt-hard economics: each fake identity ties up real capital, and unendorsed nodes hang off the trellis as isolated orphans no one will transact with.
